overview: Diageo is the world's largest premium spirits company, owning a portfolio of leading beer, spirits, and RTD brands including Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Captain Morgan, Baileys, Don Julio, Tanqueray, Crown Royal and Guinness, plus a ~34% equity stake in the Moët Hennessy luxury wines/spirits JV and a majority stake in India's United Spirits Limited (USL). The UK-incorporated, LSE-primary-listed company (NYSE ADR: DEO, 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share) sells across more than 180 countries with North America (~40% of net sales), Europe, Asia Pacific, Latin America/Caribbean, and Africa as reporting regions, and reports in US dollars since switching from GBP in FY2024. It is a 20-F filer with the SEC (CIK 835403) and fiscal year ends 30 June.

business_model.summary: Diageo manufactures, markets and distributes branded alcoholic beverages, monetizing a portfolio of premium/luxury-positioned spirits and beer brands sold through third-party distributors, wholesalers, and its own route-to-market organization in key markets. Revenue is largely volume- and price/mix-driven consumer staples-like repeat purchase, with premiumization (consumers trading up within categories) as the structural margin driver. FY2026 net sales were $19,643m, down 3.0% reported and down 2.0% organic, with reported operating profit of $3,156m (down 27.2%) due to ~$2,527m of exceptional charges (Türkiye/Mey İçki impairment ~$786m, Don Papa brand impairment ~$287m, restructuring ~$908m).

revenue_streams.name: Scotch (incl. Johnnie Walker)
revenue_streams.trend: stable/mixed - Scotch overall soft, Johnnie Walker grew organically

revenue_streams.name: Beer (incl. Guinness)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - Guinness double-digit growth in GB/Ireland

revenue_streams.name: Tequila (incl. Don Julio, Casamigos)
revenue_streams.trend: declining - category pressure, competitive US market

revenue_streams.name: US whiskey & Chinese white spirits & other

business_model.customer_type: B2B route-to-market: sells to distributors, wholesalers, retailers, and on-trade (bars/restaurants) rather than directly to consumers; heavy reliance on brand marketing to drive consumer pull
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~42% ($7,249m FY26), Europe ~30% ($5,097m), Asia Pacific ~19% ($3,333m), Latin America & Caribbean ~12.5% ($2,160m), Africa ~9.5% ($1,642m) of regional net sales (totals exceed 100% before corporate eliminations)

main_competitors: Moët Hennessy/LVMH (JV partner, also competitor in wines)
competitive_position.market_position: Global spirits market leader with roughly 19-23% global spirits market share by value, well ahead of #2 Pernod Ricard (~13% revenue scale) and far larger than Brown-Forman (~$5.4bn revenue) and Constellation (~7% share). Diageo and Pernod Ricard together dominate the premium multinational spirits category; a reported Pernod Ricard/Brown-Forman merger discussion (if consummated) would create a combined entity approaching Diageo's scale.

moat_factors.description: Owns category-leading brands across nearly every major spirits type (Scotch, tequila, vodka, gin, rum, Canadian whisky) plus Guinness in beer, diversifying category-specific demand risk
Global distribution infrastructure and scale purchasing/production give cost and shelf-placement advantages smaller rivals cannot match
Decades of marketing investment in brands like Johnnie Walker, Don Julio and Baileys support premium pricing, though this has weakened amid recent consumer trade-down
Scotch and aged whiskies require years of maturation stock, a capital and time barrier new entrants cannot quickly replicate
~34% stake gives exposure to ultra-premium champagne/cognac without full capital commitment

weaknesses: Heavy North America dependence (~40%+ of sales) during a prolonged US spirits demand slowdown and distributor destocking cycle
Tequila and vodka categories losing share to RTDs, craft/local brands, and cautious consumer trade-down
Complex emerging-market exposure (Turkey, Nigeria, Africa) brings FX volatility and hyperinflation accounting noise
Leverage elevated (~3.1x net debt/EBITDA) constrains M&A and buyback flexibility during the turnaround
Large non-controlled JV (Moët Hennessy) and majority-but-not-wholly-owned India unit (USL) create minority-interest/governance complexity

growth_drivers: Guinness capacity expansion - new Littleconnell brewery (~€300m, opened May 2026) in Kildare, Ireland, with a further ~€400m 'Brewery 2' expansion planned to more than double site capacity, supporting continued double-digit Guinness/Guinness 0.0 growth
Ready-to-drink (RTD) category expansion leveraging existing spirits brands (Smirnoff, Captain Morgan RTDs)
Premiumization - continued mix-shift toward higher-margin, higher-price-point products within each spirits category
Emerging markets - India (via United Spirits premiumization), Latin America/Caribbean, and select African markets as structural long-term volume growth regions despite near-term softness

Accelerate / operating-framework cost program - ~$1bn of targeted 3-year savings (~$850m from operating framework redesign, ~$150m from supply chain initiatives) expected to flow through FY27-FY28 margins
Portfolio pruning - EABL and RCB disposals redeploy capital/management attention toward core spirits and deleverage the balance sheet
North America turnaround under new CEO Dave Lewis, including supply-chain reshoring (closing a Canadian bottling plant to shift production closer to US customers) to mitigate tariff costs

business.risk: North America destocking and weak consumer spirits demand
business.description: US distributor/trade destocking has run ahead of underlying depletion declines; a cautious, trading-down US consumer continues to pressure volumes and mix, especially in tequila and vodka

Investor concern that GLP-1 adoption structurally reduces alcohol consumption; management says early evidence suggests lower impact on spirits than beer/wine, but the narrative remains an overhang given still-limited penetration data
Tequila and vodka facing competitive and craft-brand pressure; Scotch has had periods of decline even as Johnnie Walker specifically grows

business.risk: Execution risk on Türkiye/Mey İçki and Don Papa
business.description: FY26 impairments ($786m Türkiye, $287m Don Papa) show execution/demand misjudgments in specific brand or market bets

financial.description: Net debt $20,482m, leverage ~3.1x adjusted EBITDA versus a medium-term target band of 2.5-3x by FY27 and ~2x by FY29; constrains capital allocation flexibility until disposals close and EBITDA recovers
Reported profit decline and restructuring cash costs pressure near-term free cash flow even as operating cash flow held up ($4,392m FY26)
USD reporting since FY2024 plus hyperinflationary economies (Turkey, and historically Nigeria/Ghana) introduce material non-operating volatility to reported results

regulatory.description: Roughly 40-45% of US net sales depend on products made in Mexico (Don Julio, Casamigos tequila) or Canada (Crown Royal); management previously estimated a potential ~$200m operating profit hit from tariffs, partially mitigated via agave cost declines, productivity savings, and supply-chain reshoring
Rising global scrutiny of alcohol health warnings, minimum pricing, and advertising restrictions in various markets could structurally dampen volume growth over time
EABL sale to Asahi required Kenyan court and regulatory clearance before completion; similar approval risk applies to other portfolio disposals

macro.description: On-trade (bars/restaurants) and premium price points are more exposed to discretionary income pressure in a weaker consumer environment
Africa, Latin America, and Turkey/India exposure introduces translation risk to reported USD results
Agave (tequila), grain, glass/packaging and energy costs affect COGS, though agave costs have recently been declining, a tailwind

execution.description: Sir Dave Lewis (ex-Tesco CEO) took over January 2026 after Debra Crew's July 2025 departure and an interim period under CFO Nik Jhangiani; large-scale reorganization (new NA, EMEA, APAC leadership) carries integration/execution risk
Delivering ~$1bn of targeted 3-year savings while simultaneously executing the North America turnaround and portfolio disposals is a demanding, multi-workstream program
EABL (~$2.3bn) and RCB (~$1.78bn) disposal proceeds must be used to delever as planned rather than diverted to less accretive uses

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global premium spirits long-term structural growth from emerging-market premiumization remains intact, but the industry is mid-cycle in a cyclical/post-pandemic normalization downturn concentrated in North America; beer (led by Guinness) is currently outperforming spirits
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - alcohol demand is relatively defensive versus broader consumer discretionary categories, but premium/luxury price points and on-trade channels add cyclical sensitivity, and the current destocking cycle is adding extra volatility
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - ~$20.5bn net debt means higher rates raise refinancing cost and pressure the leverage deleveraging timeline

recent_developments.event: FY2026 results released: net sales $19,643m (-3.0% reported, -2.0% organic), operating profit down 27.2% to $3,156m on ~$2,527m exceptional charges; announced $1.2bn 2-year restructuring ('Accelerate'/operating framework redesign) targeting ~$1bn 3-year savings; stock rose ~4-8% on the cost-cutting plan despite weak headline results

New CEO Dave Lewis announced major cost-cutting and reorganization, including a $625m initial savings target later expanded into the full $1bn 3-year program; workforce reduction of nearly 2,000 roles

Opened new €300m Littleconnell brewery in Kildare, Ireland, as part of near-€1bn Irish investment program (2020-2029); confirmed plans for a further ~€400m 'Brewery 2' expansion to more than double site capacity

Kenyan court cleared the path for Diageo's ~$2.3bn sale of its East African Breweries (EABL) stake to Asahi Group Holdings, with long-term brand licensing agreements (Guinness, Smirnoff, Captain Morgan) retained

Agreed to sell controlling stake in Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) IPL cricket franchise to a Blackstone/Aditya Birla-led consortium for ~$1.78bn, part of the non-core asset disposal program to reduce debt
H1 FY2026 results showed revenue decline but Guinness sales 'soaring,' while overall dividend was cut/held flat reflecting balance-sheet discipline
Sir Dave Lewis (former Tesco Group CEO) formally began as Diageo plc CEO and Executive Director
Agreed sale of East African Breweries stake to Asahi for $2.3bn
Debra Crew stepped down as CEO after two years; CFO Nik Jhangiani served as interim CEO until Dave Lewis's start

US tariffs on Mexico/Canada-made spirits (tequila, Canadian whisky) became a focal risk; Diageo announced closure of a Crown Royal bottling facility in Ontario, Canada (by Feb 2026) to shift volume closer to US customers

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Preliminary Results / Capital Markets Day, August 2026

items.notes: North America organic net sales guided down mid-single-digit, assuming the US market itself is down ~3% with Diageo improving share performance versus FY26
Includes ~40% of the ~$850m operating-framework savings and ~25% of the ~$150m supply-chain savings landing in FY27
~$1.2bn total program cost (~$1.1bn operating framework, ~$100m supply chain), with ~$752m already incurred in FY26
Targeting further reduction toward ~2x by FY2029; FY26 actual leverage ~3.1x; EABL and RCB disposal proceeds (~$2.3bn + ~$1.78bn) earmarked for debt reduction

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Dave Lewis has framed FY2027 as a reset year prioritizing the North America turnaround, structural cost reduction, and balance-sheet deleveraging over top-line growth, while continuing to invest in Guinness capacity and premiumization in emerging markets. Management has characterized GLP-1 impact on spirits specifically as limited so far given low current penetration, distinguishing spirits from beer/wine categories.

bull_case: Global #1 spirits brand portfolio and scale route-to-market provide a durable moat that is likely to outlast the current cyclical North America destocking downturn
New CEO (Dave Lewis, proven turnaround operator from Tesco) plus a credible ~$1bn structural cost program gives a clear margin-recovery path independent of a top-line recovery
Guinness is a standout growth engine (double-digit growth, major new Irish capacity coming online) that is underappreciated relative to the spirits weakness dominating headlines
EABL and RCB disposals (~$4bn combined proceeds) materially accelerate deleveraging toward the 2.5-3x target without needing asset sales of core spirits brands
Analyst sentiment has turned more constructive (consensus 'Buy', ~30% implied upside to average price target), suggesting the destocking narrative may be largely priced in
bear_case: North America spirits demand malaise could prove more structural than cyclical if younger consumers are permanently drinking less (moderation trends, GLP-1 adoption growth, health-consciousness)
Leverage (~3.1x) limits financial flexibility during the turnaround; execution missteps (as seen in the Türkiye and Don Papa impairments) show the risk of further write-downs

Tariffs on Mexico/Canada-sourced tequila and Canadian whisky directly tax ~40%+ of US sales and could escalate further under US trade policy, pressuring North America margins just as the segment needs to stabilize
FY2027 guidance of only 'broadly flat' organic sales and continued North America decline signals the turnaround will take years, not quarters, extending a period of earnings uncertainty
Restructuring and leadership transition (third CEO change in under two years counting the interim period) carries integration and culture-execution risk at a critical juncture
